newsitem.title: switzerland: Swiss shares end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end little changed.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares ended little changed with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) breaking off a four-day record run to end slightly below its Monday close.

The fact that the SMI ended lower despite an early all-time high at 4,734.1 points showed how nervous the market was at the current levels, a dealer said. Profit taking and early Wall Street weakness were seen behind the weaker close. All-share Swiss Performace (SPI) ended marginally higher.
The outlook remained favourable due to the lack of alternative investment, one trader noted.
* The SMI down 7.3 points, or 0.16 percent, to 4,677.1.
* All-share SPI was up 1.29 points, or 0.04 percent, to 2,9060.32. Volume was high with more than 3.3 billion francs' worth in shares traded on the bourse.

* Attention concentrated on share rights in Ciba Specialty ended two francs higher at 103.50 after an early slump to 92.50 francs. On Monday night, a bank consortium said it would bid 90 francs per subscription right. Trade in shares in Ciba Specialty Holding, which is being spun off from Novartis, will begin on Thursday.

* UBS bearers added seven francs to 1,355. Dealers said rumours that UBS held a nine percent stake in German DePfa-BAnk AG had no effect on the price. UBS denied renewed claims by DePfa that UBS held a nine percent stake.
* Credit Suisse Group jumped four francs to 170. SBC, which is to release its 1996 results on Wednesday, slid four francs to 303 due to profit taking.
* Alusuisse and Sulzer posted gains of more than one percent. Second-tier Schindler registereds added 105 francs to 1,640 after releasing postitive results.

* Trade was temporarily frantic on Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex) due to large fluctuations on the cash market. Dealers said big price swings in Novartis shares and share rights on Ciba Specialty Chemicals was a factor influencing Soffex prices.
In total, 141,486 options were traded with a call put ratio of 1.29 to one. UBS options saw good demand.
Volume in SMI options reached 38,570 contracts and 6,926 contracts in SMI futures.
